name: High-to-Low Cable Woodchopper
alternative_names: Diagonal Cable Chop High to Low
description: The high-to-low cable woodchopper trains diagonal trunk rotation in a downward arc, emphasizing the external oblique on the pulling side and the contralateral internal oblique. The diagonal movement pattern closely replicates the biomechanics of a downward striking action used in chopping, overhead throwing follow-through, and many racquet-sport movements. The continuous cable tension challenges both the rotational prime movers and the hip stabilizers throughout a large three-dimensional arc.

execution.starting_position: Set the cable pulley to its highest position. Stand side-on to the machine, grasping the handle with both hands above and outside the shoulder closest to the stack.
execution.setup_instructions: Attach a rope or single handle to the high pulley. Stand far enough away that the cable is loaded at the start.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms extended upward toward the cable, torso rotated toward the stack.
Step 2: Pull the handle diagonally downward and across the body in a chopping arc, rotating the torso away from the cable.
Step 3: Finish with the handle outside the far hip, knees slightly bent and weight shifted.
Step 4: Resist the cable and return in a controlled arc to the start position.
Step 5: Complete all reps then switch sides.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale forcefully on the downward chop. Inhale on the controlled return upward.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows — the movement should originate from the trunk, not the arms
Squatting down instead of rotating — the squat component should be minimal
safety_considerations: Keep the spine neutral throughout — avoid lateral spinal flexion
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full diagonal arc from high outside one shoulder to low outside the opposite hip.
coaching_cues: Imagine swinging an axe — the power comes from the whole trunk
